items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I learned a lot from his recordings. I listened to his articulation.

ctx.x: Richie. Yeah, he passed with that, too.

So Bud was staying in Richie’s place and he wasn’t far from me. He played my piano. I invited my hero and I said, “You want to play a few notes? Great!” (laughs) Because I loved his recordings anyway. He would be standing outside listening to the jam sessions we were having. My hero is outside listening and then he would walk away, he’d stay and listen. He was going through some psychological things you know, but he was a genius. So I learned a lot from his recordings. I listened to his articulation.
So you were already listening to jazz pianists but you weren’t really playing jazz you were playing R&B.
